analysis.title: Baker Hughes Company 3Q26 Quick Look – OFSE Leads EBITDA Beat, IET Orders Crush Again
key_insights: BKR 3Q26 Adjusted EBITDA of $1,415mm was 5% above Barclays and 5% above consensus, led by OFSE with upside from Chart's first partial quarter.
OFSE segment EBITDA of $659mm was 6% above Barclays and 5% above consensus. OFSE margin rose 47bps q/q to 18.0% on higher volume and pricing.
Total revenue of $8,025mm was 3% above both Barclays and consensus, helped by Chart's first partial quarter. Chart EBITDA margin was 150bps above Barclays' estimate.
FCF of $734mm was well ahead of Barclays' $276mm estimate.
IET orders of $5.9bn were well above consensus, led by a 1.1 GW data center order from a major U.S. tech company. The award pairs 43 NovaLT and Frame 5 turbine packages with BRUSH generators.

A second ~500 MW data center order also uses BRUSH generators, bringing 3Q AI power awards to about 1.6 GW. Barclays thinks Brush is underappreciated because owning the generator lets BKR sell a complete power package and grows the installed base for higher-margin aftermarket work.
Other IET awards included LNG orders (Venture Global's Plaquemines expansion and Cloud Connector pipeline) and a record quarter for compressor upgrades. IET RPO hit a record $39.4bn.

BKR raised its Horizon 2 target to $50bn+ and management called the upstream market inflecting, citing record RPO, a robust order pipeline, a growing installed base and an inflecting energy upstream market.

SLB's first look at 2027 assumed mid single-digit global activity growth with no Middle East recovery (held flat at 2H26 levels). HAL and WFRD framed 2027 the same way, and all three came out roughly in line with consensus. Barclays expects BKR sees the market the same way, with any Middle East normalization adding OFSE upside.

Chart beat in its first quarter: revenue and EBITDA were 6% and 16% above Barclays, and the margin beat the ~17% 2H outlook. Chart orders were 8% below Barclays. Chart's cold boxes were included in the Plaquemines award, an early cross-sell example.

FY26 EBITDA guidance was raised to a $5.265bn midpoint including Chart, 2% above consensus. 4Q revenue and EBITDA guidance are in line with consensus, with continued Middle East disruption built in. FY26 FCF conversion is still guided to 45-50%.
Barclays rates BKR Equal Weight with a $72 price target (12.5x 2027E EBITDA, current net debt) versus a $59.00 close on 27-Oct-2026, implying 22.0% upside. Industry view is Positive.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays kept Equal Weight and a $72 target after a 3Q26 beat on EBITDA and IET orders. The target is based on 12.5x 2027E EBITDA and current net debt.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays' industry view is Positive, with fundamentals and valuations improving. Management and peers describe the upstream market as inflecting, with mid single-digit global activity growth expected in 2027.

earnings_insights: BKR 3Q26 reported Adjusted EBITDA $1,415mm vs Barclays est $1,344mm and consensus est $1,342mm, up 15% q/q and 14% y/y.
BKR 3Q26 reported total revenue $8,025mm vs Barclays est $7,820mm and consensus est $7,794mm.

BKR 3Q26 reported OFSE revenue $3,660mm vs Barclays est $3,599mm and consensus est $3,583mm. Reported OFSE EBITDA $659mm vs Barclays est $623mm and consensus est $628mm, with OFSE margin 18.0% vs consensus est 17.5%.
BKR 3Q26 reported IET revenue $3,477mm vs Barclays est $3,381mm and consensus est $3,345mm. Reported IET EBITDA $685mm vs Barclays est $666mm and consensus est $663mm, with IET margin 19.7%.
BKR 3Q26 reported Chart revenue $888mm and EBITDA $156mm (17.6% margin) in its first partial quarter, vs Barclays est EBITDA $135mm (16.1% margin) and consensus est EBITDA $140mm.

BKR 3Q26 reported IET orders $5,886mm vs Barclays est $3,970mm and consensus est $3,630mm. Reported Chart orders $831mm vs Barclays est $900mm and consensus est $1,059mm. Reported total orders $10,764mm vs Barclays est $8,566mm and consensus est $8,014mm.
BKR 3Q26 reported free cash flow $734mm vs Barclays est $276mm and consensus est $265mm. Cash from operations was $1,005mm and capex $271mm.
BKR 3Q26 reported net debt $14,196mm (net debt/capital 40.8%) vs $526mm in 2Q26, and cash and equivalents $4,068mm. ROIC was 7.6%.

BKR FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to a $5.265bn midpoint including Chart, 2% above consensus. FY26 Chart EBITDA guidance was maintained, 4Q guidance is in line with consensus, and FCF conversion guidance is 45-50%. The earnings call is at 9:30am ET on 28 October 2026.
risk_factors: Greater competition in the OFSE segment.
Lower demand for LNG and oil & gas, which would significantly decrease BKR's IET orders.
Global E&P spending slowing meaningfully in 2026, resulting in lower Digital adoption.
Continued Middle East disruption and unknowns around 2027 OFSE activity.
geopolitical: Middle East disruption continues to be built into BKR's 4Q outlook. SLB's 2027 view assumes no Middle East recovery from 2H26 levels, and any normalization would add OFSE upside.
